l-m-m1-b01-07.title: Rule for Knowing Whether Fraction Be Integer
l-m-m1-b01-07.goal: Decide which information you really need to know whether fraction be integer, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-m1-b01-07.material: We wan arrange 6/3, 3/4, and 7/2 into "whole numbers" and "rational numbers wey no be whole numbers." Think about the real rule wey we need.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the real rule we need to arrange dem?
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.o.a: Calculate am and see whether e give whole-number value.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.o.b: Check whether the top number pass the bottom number.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.r.b: 7/2 no be whole number, even though the top number pass the bottom one.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.o.c: Treat am as no be whole number if e look like fraction.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.r.c: Even if e look like fraction, e fit be whole number, like 6/3=2.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.o.d: Check whether the bottom number na odd number.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.r.d: You no fit know whether e be whole number by checking if the bottom number na even or odd.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s1.explain: 6/3=2 na whole number, while 3/4 and 7/2 na rational numbers wey no be whole numbers. Na only when you calculate the value you go know.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s2.model.0: The rule na whether the fraction give whole number after calculation, so 6/3=2 na whole number.
l-m-m1-b01-07.s.s2.model.1: Even if the form na fraction, the value fit be whole number, so you need calculate am to check.

l-m-m1-b05-37.material: Dem find median for data 12, 5, 9, 20, 7, 15 this way. ① There be 6 values, so find the mean of the middle two ② The middle two values na 9 and 20 ③ (9+20)÷2=14.5 ④ Median na 14.5

l-m-m1-b0s4-09.goal: Follow the solution for number of sides of regular polygon with inner angle 150°, or the cause-and-effect chain, step by step. Find the first wrong part and fix am.
l-m-m1-b0s4-09.material: Dem find number of sides for regular polygon with inner angle 150° like this. ① One outer angle na 180°−150°=30° ② Sum of outer angles na 180°, so sides na 180÷30=6 ③ Therefore na regular hexagon.
l-m-m1-b0s4-09.s.s1.r.a: Inner and outer angles add up to 180°, so 30° correct.

l-m-m1-b0s4-09.s.s1.r.d: Inner angle for regular hexagon na 120°, wey no match 150°.
l-m-m1-b0s4-09.s.s1.explain: Sum of outer angles of polygon na 360°. 360÷30=12, so na regular dodecagon.
l-m-m1-b0s4-09.s.s2.model.0: Sum of outer angles na 360°, no be 180°, so ② wrong and 360÷30=12 correct.
l-m-m1-b0s4-09.s.s2.model.1: Inner angle for regular hexagon na 120°, so 6 wrong; using 360° in ② give regular dodecagon.

l-m-m1-b01-26.title: Writing item prices as expression with letters
l-m-m1-b01-26.goal: Change the situation of buying things into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-m1-b01-26.material: Dem buy 5 sweets at x won each and 3 jellies at y won each. Make we change the amount paid into expression wey use letters.
l-m-m1-b01-26.s.s1.prompt: Which expression show the money wey dem pay?

l-m-m1-b01-26.s.s1.r.c: Dem exchange the prices of sweets and jellies.
l-m-m1-b01-26.s.s1.r.d: Dem add the numbers instead of multiplying dem.
l-m-m1-b01-26.s.s1.explain: The sweets na 5 pieces at x won each, so dem cost 5x won. The jellies na 3 pieces at y won each, so dem cost 3y won. Together, e na 5x+3y won.

l-m-m1-b01-26.s.s2.model.1: You need multiply the number by the price of one item, then add. So 5x+3y won get the same meaning.

l-m-m1-b01-27.goal: Change the situation where temperature drop into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.

l-m-m1-b01-27.s.s2.model.1: When you add the change −7 to starting temperature +5, you get evening temperature −2. So dem describe the same situation.

l-m-m1-b01-28.title: Changing sentence into equation
l-m-m1-b01-28.goal: Change a condition wey sentence give into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-m1-b01-28.material: Sentence: 'The value of 3 times a number minus 4 is equal to the number plus 8.' Make the number x and change the sentence into equation.
l-m-m1-b01-28.s.s1.prompt: Which equation get the same meaning as the sentence?
l-m-m1-b01-28.s.s1.r.a: E talk say 'the value of 3 times minus 4', but dem multiply (x−4) by 3.
l-m-m1-b01-28.s.s1.r.d: Dem write 'the value of the number plus 8' as 8x.
l-m-m1-b01-28.s.s1.explain: '3 times the number minus 4' na 3x−4, and 'the number plus 8' na x+8.

l-m-m1-b01-28.s.s2.model.1: Dem change every part of the sentence into expression in order, so 3x−4=x+8 get the same meaning.

l-m-m1-b01-29.s.s2.model.1: When length increase, width suppose reduce so the area go remain 12. So y=12/x correct.

l-m-m1-b01-30.title: Changing cylinder into net
l-m-m1-b01-30.goal: Change the curved surface of a cylinder into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-m1-b01-30.material: Draw the net for cylinder wey base radius na 3 cm. The side surface na rectangle. Make we think of the solid as shape wey dem open flat.
l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s1.prompt: How long the horizontal side of the rectangle side surface be?
l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s1.r.a: Dem leave out π. Circumference na π times diameter 6.
l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s1.r.c: Dem mistake area formula like π×r² for length.

l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s1.explain: The horizontal side of the side surface equal the circumference of the base circle. 2π×3=6π cm.
l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s2.model.0: When dem open the side surface flat, the horizontal side equal the base circumference, so 2π×3=6π cm.
l-m-m1-b01-30.s.s2.model.1: Because the side surface wrap round the base circle once, the horizontal side na the circle circumference, 6π cm.

l-m-m1-b05-22.material: I wan change relationship y=20/x into table. Write y values in order when x na 1, 2, 4, and 5.
l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s1.prompt: Which table show the same relationship as this equation?
l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s1.r.a: As x dey increase, y too dey increase. This na table for direct proportion y=20x.
l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s1.r.c: This na table for y=20−x. Product x×y no stay constant.
l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s1.r.d: This na table for y=x+20. E no be inverse proportion.

l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s2.model.0: Putting x=1, 2, 4, 5 into y=20÷x give 20, 10, 5, 4, so the table match the equation.
l-m-m1-b05-22.s.s2.model.1: Product x and y always na 20, so when x become 2 times bigger, y become half.

l-m-m1-b05-30.s.s2.model.1: Two angles side by side make straight angle, wey be 180°. When you solve, x=50.

l-m-m1-b0s4-11.title: Turn line description into equation
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.goal: Change line through origin into equation y=ax, another way to show am (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why meanings same.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.material: One line pass through origin. Each time point on this line move 3 squares right, e move up 6 squares. Change the line into equation y=ax.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be equation for this line?
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s1.r.a: You use 3 squares right as a. a mean how many times y be x.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s1.r.b: You use 6 squares up as a. When x=3, y must be 6.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s1.r.d: You swap x and y roles. If x=3, y must be 6.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s1.explain: When x=3, y=6, so y na 2 times x. a=6÷3=2, so y=2x.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s2.model.0: When x=3, y=6, so a=6÷3=2 and y=2x.
l-m-m1-b0s4-11.s.s2.model.1: For every 1 square right, e go 2 squares up, so y na 2 times x, meaning y=2x.

l-m-m1-b0s4-12.title: Say midpoint as length equation
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.goal: Change midpoint of segment into equation of lengths, another way to express am (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why meaning same.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.material: Point B dey on segment AC and na the midpoint. Use length AB to express length AC as equation.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s1.r.a: Midpoint divide segment into 2 equal parts, no be 3.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s1.r.b: AB na half of AC, so dem no equal.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s1.r.c: AB na half of AC, so AC na 2 times AB. You turn am the other way round.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s1.explain: Midpoint divide segment into two parts with equal lengths. AB=BC, so AC=AB+BC=2×AB.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s2.model.0: B na midpoint, so AB=BC. Therefore AC=AB+BC=2×AB.
l-m-m1-b0s4-12.s.s2.model.1: AB na half of AC, so AC na 2 times AB, meaning AC=2×AB.

l-m-m1-b01-31.title: Which of the two solutions give the least common multiple?
l-m-m1-b01-31.goal: Compare the two methods or claims in the two solutions to find the least common multiple of 36 and 60, choose the better one, and explain why.
l-m-m1-b01-31.material: Dem find the least common multiple of 36 and 60 in two ways. A: 36=2²×3², 60=2²×3×5, so 2²×3²×5=180. B: 36×60=2160.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s1.prompt: Which solution find the least common multiple correctly?
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s1.r.a: 2160 na common multiple, but e no be the smallest common multiple.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s1.r.b: 2160 na 12 times 180, so e no be the least.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s1.r.c: 180 truly na the least common multiple of 36 and 60.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s1.explain: 180 na 5 times 36 and 3 times 60, and na the smallest common multiple. The product of the two numbers no be the least.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s2.model.0: A find 180 by multiplying each prime factor once with the bigger power, so na the least common multiple.
l-m-m1-b01-31.s.s2.model.1: B's 2160 na common multiple, but 180 fit divide am, so e no be the least.

l-m-m1-b01-32.s.s1.r.a: B solve am correctly too: from 2x+6=14, 2x=8 and x=4.
l-m-m1-b01-32.s.s1.r.b: A solve am correctly too by dividing both sides by 2.
l-m-m1-b01-32.s.s1.r.d: Put x=4 inside and you get 2×7=14, so e correct.

l-m-m1-b01-32.s.s2.model.0: Both methods give x=4, and putting am inside also give 14, so both correct.
l-m-m1-b01-32.s.s2.model.1: Even if the order of solving different, dem follow equality rules, so the same answer come out.

l-m-m1-b01-34.s.s2.model.0: If base remain the same, volume dey proportional to height, so when height become 2 times, volume also become 2 times.
l-m-m1-b01-34.s.s2.model.1: If radius become 2 times, area πr² become 4 times, so B no correct and na only A correct.

l-m-m1-b05-31.title: Constructing equilateral triangle: comparing 2 methods
l-m-m1-b05-31.goal: Compare two ways to construct equilateral triangle on line segment AB, choose the better way, and explain your thinking.
l-m-m1-b05-31.material: Construct equilateral triangle with line segment AB as one side. M: Draw arcs with radius AB from A and B, and call their meeting point C. N: Set C using arcs with same radius, longer than AB, from A and B.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s1.r.b: The radius longer than AB, so AC and BC longer than AB.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s1.r.c: N make isosceles triangle where only AC=BC.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s1.r.d: For M, all three sides equal AB.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s1.explain: For M, AC and BC equal compass radius AB, so all three sides equal. N make isosceles triangle with AC=BC>AB.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s2.model.0: For M, AC and BC equal radius AB, so e be equilateral triangle with three equal sides.
l-m-m1-b05-31.s.s2.model.1: For N, AC and BC longer than AB, so the three sides no equal and e no be equilateral triangle.

l-m-m1-b0s4-13.title: Compare two ways to find sector area
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.goal: Compare two methods or claims to find sector area, choose better one, and explain your reason.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.material: Arc length of sector with radius 10 cm and central angle 72° na 4π cm. Method 1: 100π×72/360=20π. Method 2: ½×radius×arc length=½×10×4π=20π. Both methods get same answer.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.prompt: Which statement compare the two methods correctly?
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.o.a: Only Method 1 correct, and Method 2 na coincidence
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.r.a: If you know arc length, Method 2 also be formula wey always work.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.o.b: Both correct, and if you know arc length, Method 2 convenient
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.r.c: Method 1 also correct because sector na part of circle.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.o.d: The answers same, so you no need know central angle
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.r.d: Method 2 also need central angle to find arc length.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s1.explain: Both methods correct and give same answer. If you only know central angle, Method 1 simpler; if you already know arc length, Method 2 simpler.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s2.model.0: Both methods give 20π and correct, so if you already know arc length, Method 2 convenient because na one multiplication.
l-m-m1-b0s4-13.s.s2.model.1: Method 1 correct because e take 72/360 of circle, and Method 2 formula treat sector like triangle, so e quicker if arc length known.
